command line: msta [ options ...] specification-file

YACC compatible options:
  `-d', `-define'  Create the header file.
  `-l', `-line'    Produce code without #line constructs.
  `-t', `-trace'   Permit compilation of debugging code in the code file.
  `-v', `-verbose' Write a file containing description of the parser.
  `-b file_prefix' Use file_prefix instead of y as the prefix for all
                   output filenames (y.tab.c, y.tab.h, y.output).
  `-p sym_prefix'  Use sym_prefix instead of yy as the prefix for all
                   external names produced by yacc.

New options: Default options are marked by star (*).
  `-h', `-help', or `--help'
                   Output this message
  `-w'             Inhibit all warning messages
  `-c++'           Generate c++ code instead of c
  `-enum'          Generate token constants as enumeration instead of macro
* `-no-enum'       Generate token constants as macro
* `-pattern-equiv' Equiv patterns are denoted by the same nonterminal
  `-no-pattern-equiv'
                   Equiv patterns are denoted by different nonterminals and
                   are expanded into the different set of rules
  `-look-ahead number'
  `-la number'
                   Define k (default value: 1) for LR(k)-,LALR(k)-grammars.
  `-lr'            Input grammar is considered as LR(k)-grammar.
* `-no-lr'         Input grammar is considered as LALR(k)-grammar.
* `-lalr-optimization'
                   Extract LALR parts of input LR(k)-grammar and represent
                   them by adequate LR-sets (only when option -lr is on)
  `-no-lalr-optimization'
                   Option is opposite to the previous one.
* `-regular-optimization'
                   Extract regular parts of input grammar and implement them
                   by adequate methods (deterministic finite automaton).
  `-no-regular-optimization'
                   Option is opposite to the previous one.
  `-split-lr-sets' Splitting LR-sets during regular optimization
                   in order to extract more regular parts (only when option
                   -regular-optimization is on).  Default if %scanner
                   is present
  `-no-split-lr-sets'
                   Option is opposite to the previous one.  Default if
                   %scanner is absent
* `-yacc-error-recovery'
                   Use error recover according to Posix YACC standard.
  `-local-error-recovery'
                   Use a local error recovery method.
  `-minimal-error-recovery'
                   Use minimal error recovery method.
* `-error-reduce'
                   Permits default reduces on error.
  `-no-error-reduce'
                   Reduces on error only for the right lookahead.
* `-error-conflict'
                   Permits reporting conflicts on error.
  `-no-error-conflict'
                   Do not report conflicts on errors.
  `-yacc-input'    Only Posix YACC input can be used as input grammar.
* `-no-yacc-input' All input grammar features of MSTA can be used.
  `-strict'        Use only strict POSIX YACC input (when `-yacc-input')
                   not SYSTEM V one.  Errors are output when nonstrict
                   features are used.
* `-no-strict'     When `-yacc-input', only warnings about non strict POSIX
                   YACC features usage are output.
  `-yacc-file-names'
                   Output file names are generated according to Posix YACC.
* `-no-yacc-file-names'
                   Output files will have the same name and suffixes (.h,
                   .c, and .output).
  `-o name'        Specify names of output files (header file name.h,
                   code file name.c(name.cpp), description file name.output)
  `-y', `-yacc'    Emulate Posix YACC.  It means that the options -no-enum
                   -yacc-input, -lalr, -yacc-error-recovery, -error-reduce,
                   -error-conflict and -yacc-file-names are on.
  `-full-lr-set'   Write full LR-sets into a file containing description
                   of the parser (the option acts only with option -v).
  `-lr-situation-context'
                   Write context of LR-situations into description of the
                   parser (the option acts only with option -v).
  `-removed-lr-sets'
                   Write LR-sets removed during conflict resolution and
                   regular optimization into description of the
                   parser (the option acts only with option -v).
* `-expand'        Attributes & states in the parser will be expandable.
  `-no-expand'     Option is opposite to the previous one.
  `-time'          Output time statistics into stderr.
  `-debug number'  Output debug information (with given level>=0) into stderr.
